course_description:
Cognitive neuroscience is an emerging field of inquiry concerned with how the brain accomplishes tasks such as remembering, sensory perception and language. This course will provide a survey of topics in cognitive neuroscience with a focus on how neuroscience has advanced our understanding of the brain, as well as the methodologies used to gain these insights.

Cognitive neuroscience is an exciting and influential field of inquiry concerned with how the brain accomplishes conscious and unconscious tasks such as sensory perception, learning, representing the body and the environment, and interacting with other people.

Following from NEUR2020, you will learn to programme sections of a cognitive task in Matlab, collect data from participants with that programme, process and analyse the data, which will form the basis for a short report (written and submitted in class, in two parts).ﾠThis will encourage you to think logically and analytically, and prepare you for the research demands of fourth (honours) year. Your assessment tasks will be the sections of MATLAB programme you have coded and collection of data from some participants on a (fun!) task which will investigate gaze cueing and shifts of attention when we look at people versus cats. You will report on that analysed data, and will complete two multiple-choice quizzes on the lecture material.ﾠﾠ

Tutorials will be conducted in computer labs. Some tutorial material will be pre-recorded and made available on Blackboard in the first week. It is essential that these materials are studied prior to commencing the tutorial course.

course_aims: This course aims to establish a knowledge of cognitive principles, and their evaluation through neuroscientific methodologies. Importantly, acknowledging that cognition evolves through the lifespan, this course integrates child, adolescent and adult cognitive development, and its neuroanatomical underpinnings. We include cutting-edge issues such as epigenetics, neuroprosthetics, and brain-to-brain interaction. The tutorial activities aim to complement and extend the lecture course.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the principles of the neuroanatomical basis of cognitive functions
apply the principles of cognitive neuroscience to child, adolescent and adult populations
understand how to operationalise cognitive mechanisms to enable their measurement and study
Communicate research findings from an independently-conducted project
